extracted.intended_audience: Offshore renewable energy developers, leaseholders, grant applicants, operators, and their legal/compliance teams (entities interacting with BOEM/ONRR)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and evaluation criteria for obtaining, maintaining, modifying, and relinquishing BOEM offshore renewable energy leases, grants, and associated plans (SAP, COP, GAP), payments, and financial assurance. Focuses on procedural deadlines, content requirements, financial obligations, and BOEM discretionary determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal length limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Renewal will not exceed the original operations period unless a longer time is negotiated by the parties. For limited leases, the length of the renewal will not exceed the original operations period.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOEM consideration factors for renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.429(g): BOEM will consider 'Other relevant factors, as appropriate' in deciding whether to renew a lease or grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an open-ended catch-all allowing BOEM to weigh additional relevant considerations beyond enumerated criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lease or grant termination rule
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.432(a): A lease or grant terminates on the expiration of the applicable period unless extended under §585.235(b) or §585.236(b), a renewal request is pending BOEM decision, or the lease or grant is suspended or renewed as provided; in those cases it terminates on the date set forth in the notice of suspension or renewal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Termination timing is controlled by expiration except as specifically extended, suspended, or pending renewal; notice controls the termination date when suspension/renewal occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relinquishment procedure and continuing obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.435(a): To surrender a lease, grant, or designated subdivision you must file a properly completed official relinquishment form available on the BOEM website; relinquishment takes effect on BOEM's receipt of the completed form, subject to continued obligations of the lessee or grant holder and the surety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continued obligations include: (1) make all payments due (including accrued rent and deferred bonuses), (2) decommission all facilities to BOEM's satisfaction, (3) perform any other outstanding obligations under the lease or grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: ONRR billing after relinquishment
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.435(b): After submission of a completed relinquishment form, ONRR will bill you for any outstanding payments that have accrued from obligations arising under the relinquished lease or grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM acceptance of relinquishment does not eliminate past monetary obligations; ONRR handles billing for outstanding payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reoffering or restarting leasing after relinquishment/contract/cancellation
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.438(a): If a lease or grant (or portion) is relinquished, contracted, or cancelled, BOEM may restart the competitive leasing process at any point set forth in §585.210 (e.g., RFI, Call, area identification, PSN, or FSN), subject to necessary environmental analyses and consultations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM has discretion to resume competitive leasing at the most appropriate procedural stage and must satisfy environmental/consultation requirements before reoffering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reoffer to next highest bidder within six months
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.438(b): If a competitively issued lease or grant is relinquished or cancelled within six months of the auction, BOEM may reoffer the lease or grant (or portion) to the next highest bidder from that auction, if identifiable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reoffered to next highest bidder, the price will be the next best bid or a prorated amount based on relinquished share size, provided the next best bid reflects a fair return to the government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required electronic payment mechanism and receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.500(a): For acquisition fees or the initial 12 months' rent paid for the preliminary period you must make electronic payments through the Fees for Services page on the BOEM website and include one copy of the Pay.gov confirmation receipt page with your unsolicited request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payments for acquisition and initial rents must be made electronically via BOEM's specified portal and accompanied by Pay.gov confirmation to validate payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial payments for competitively issued leases (deposits and balance)
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.500(c)/(§585.501): For competitively issued leases BOEM may require a bid deposit before the auction as established in the Final Sale Notice (FSN). The provisional auction winner must pay the balance of its accepted bid in accordance with the FSN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amounts and timing for bid deposits and bonus/balance payments are set in the FSN and binding on bidders/winners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisition fee for non-competitive leases
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.502(2): Acquisition Fee for non-competitively issued leases is $0.25 per acre, unless otherwise set by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director retains authority to set a different acquisition fee where specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial rent for commercial leases
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.503(a): The rent for a commercial lease is $3 per acre per year, unless otherwise established in the FSN or lease. You must pay the first 12 months' rent no later than 45 calendar days after receiving your executed lease copy from BOEM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FSN or lease may override the default $3/acre rate; payment timing is strict (45 days after receipt of lease copy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent rent requirements for commercial leases
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.503(a)(2) and §585.500 table: You must pay rent at the beginning of each subsequent 1‑year period for the entire lease area until the facility begins commercial operations as specified in §585.506 or otherwise specified in the FSN or lease; default amount $3 per acre per year unless otherwise provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For competitively or noncompetitively issued leases BOEM may specify adjustments to rent during the operations period and before commercial operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project easement rent timing and amount
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.500 table and §585.507(a): For a project easement the rent is the greater of $5 per acre per year or $450 per year (unless specified otherwise). First rent payment is made when the operations period begins; thereafter annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project easement size is determined per §585.628(g)(1); rent commencement is tied to operations period/BOEM approval of COP/GAP as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating fee for producing commercial leases
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.500 table and §585.506: If your commercial lease is producing, you must pay an operating fee determined by the formula in §585.506, paid annually as provided in 30 CFR 1218.51.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operating fee formula and commencement date will be specified in the lease; ONRR administers operating fee payments per referenced CFR.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROW and RUE grant rent requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.500 table and §585.508: Initial rent for ROW grants and RUE grants is the greater of $5 per acre per year or $450 per year unless otherwise established in the grant (due at grant execution); subsequent rent is due annually or in 5-year batches as provided in 30 CFR 1218.51.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant-specific terms may override default amounts or timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOEM may require bid deposits and acceptance rules for auctions
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.501: BOEM may require a bid deposit before the auction as established in the FSN; provisional winner must pay accepted bid balance per FSN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FSN governs auction financial requirements and winner payment obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and content requirements for COP rent/operating fee commencement
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.503(b): After lease begins commercial operations or on date BOEM specifies in the lease, you must pay operating fees in amount specified in §585.506. BOEM will specify in the lease the date when operating fees commence regardless of award method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operating fee start date is contractual in the lease; lessee must comply with lease-specified dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payments when developing lease in phases
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.504 introductory text: If you develop your commercial lease in BOEM-approved phases per your COP under §585.629, you must pay ONRR as provided in 30 CFR 1218.51.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phased development does not remove obligation to pay rents/fees; payment handling follows referenced CFR and BOEM approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited lease rent annual payment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.505(c): For limited leases you must pay ONRR the rent due at the beginning of each subsequent 1-year period on the entire lease area for the duration of your operations period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited leases follow a full-area annual rent payment model tied to the operations period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default operating fee rate for electricity generation
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.506(c)(1): Unless BOEM specifies otherwise, the operating fee rate 'r' is 0.02 for each year the operating fee applies when you begin commercial generation of electricity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM may specify a different rate in the lease; the 0.02 default applies unless adjusted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project easement sizing cross-reference
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.507(a)(1): The size of the project easement will be determined according to §585.628(g)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project easement rent obligations depend on area determined under referenced sizing rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director discretion to defer, reduce, or waive payments
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.510(a): The BOEM Director may defer, reduce, or waive rent, operating fee, or components of the operating fee when the Director determines continued activities would be uneconomic without relief, or necessary to encourage continued or additional activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relief is discretionary and tied to economic viability or policy goals of encouraging activity; scope includes fee rate or capacity factor components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application criteria for deferral/reduction/waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.510(b)(4)(i–ii): When requesting relief, an application must show either (i) continued activities would be uneconomic without the requested deferral/reduction/waiver, or (ii) the relief is necessary to encourage additional activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must substantiate economic hardship or public-policy/industry-growth justification; BOEM evaluates these claims in deciding relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on duration of full operating fee waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.510(c): No more than 6 years of your operations period will be subject to a full waiver of the operating fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even where BOEM grants full waivers, the total duration of such full waivers cannot exceed six years of the operations period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial assurance amount at lease execution or assignment (commercial/limited/ROW/RUE)
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.516(a)(1) and §585.520: Before BOEM will execute a commercial lease or approve an assignment (and before executing limited lease, ROW grant, or RUE grant), you or a proposed assignee must provide a bond or other authorized financial assurance in the amount of 12 months' rent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The initial financial assurance baseline is 12 months' rent for execution/assignment across commercial, limited, ROW, and RUE instruments unless otherwise specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental financial assurance for SAP/COP facility installation
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.516(a)(2–3): To install facilities approved in an SAP or COP BOEM requires a supplemental bond or other authorized financial assurance in an amount determined by BOEM based on anticipated decommissioning costs of the proposed facilities. Incremental funding schedules require BOEM approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental amounts are facility-specific and tied to BOEM's decommissioning cost estimates; BOEM approval is required for incremental funding schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial assurance must guarantee compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.516(b): Each bond or other authorized financial assurance must guarantee compliance with this part, the applicable plan approvals, and the terms and conditions of the lease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial assurance secures not just payment obligations but compliance with regulatory and plan terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hydrokinetic supplemental assurance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.516(c): For hydrokinetic commercial leases, BOEM may require supplemental financial assurance in an amount determined by BOEM prior to installation of facilities pursuant to a FERC license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hydrokinetic projects may trigger additional pre-installation financial assurance tied to FERC-licensed activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: How BOEM determines supplemental financial assurance amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.517(a): BOEM determines supplemental financial assurance amounts based on estimated costs to meet all accrued lease obligations, including: (1) projected annual rent and other payments due over next 12 months (if not covered by initial assurance), (2) any past due rent and other payments, (3) other monetary obligations, and (4) estimated cost of facility decommissioning required by subpart J.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM's calculation is forward-looking and comprehensive; decommissioning costs are explicitly included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjustment process for supplemental financial assurance
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.517(b): BOEM may adjust the supplemental financial assurance if cumulative potential obligations/liabilities change. BOEM will notify you of proposed adjustments and give an opportunity to comment; BOEM may approve a reduced amount if requested and sufficient to cover obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operators have procedural rights (notice, comment) when BOEM proposes upward adjustments and may request reductions subject to BOEM's determination of sufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial assurance changes as activities progress on limited leases/grants
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.521: BOEM may require increases or allow decreases to financial assurance based on estimated costs to meet accrued obligations. Total must be no less than amounts to cover projected rent and payments for next 12 months, past due amounts, other monetaries, and estimated decommissioning costs. BOEM will notify and provide opportunity to object if it proposes adjustments. You may request reductions if proposed amount covers obligations; BOEM may approve in its discretion. You can satisfy increases by increasing existing bond or providing supplemental assurance meeting §§585.525–585.529; incremental funding requires BOEM approval of schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial assurance for limited leases/grants is dynamic and tied to evolving obligations; procedural steps and acceptable mechanisms are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible financial instruments (non-exhaustive) and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.526(a): BOEM allows instruments other than surety bonds, including (2) pledge of cash deposited and maintained in a Federal depository account, (7) letters of credit subject to specific conditions, (8) another BOEM-approved form of security, or (9) combinations of these instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letter of credit conditions include: issuer credit rating >= investment grade from S&P or Moody's or BOEM-determined proxy; BOEM authority to demand immediate payment on default; irrevocability during term and subject to collection if not replaced 30 days before expiration; expiration at least 1 year after effective date; automatic renewal for not less than 1-year periods absent 90-day cancellation notice to BOEM; venue provision requiring disputes adjudicated in a U.S. Federal court mutually agreed by BOEM and issuer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party guaranty criteria and obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.528(a),(c): You may use a third-party guaranty to secure all or part of obligations if guarantor meets legal and financial qualifications in §§585.106 and 585.107 and submits an agreement meeting §585.528(c) criteria. All parties are bound jointly and severally, guaranty must include confession of judgment, and guarantor must meet qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If lessee or operator default, guarantor must not challenge BOEM's default determination and must remedy default; guarantor must either take corrective action or provide sufficient funds within 7 calendar days (or other agreed period) up to the guaranty's value for BOEM to complete corrective action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lease- or grant-specific decommissioning account funding rules
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.529(a)(2–3): A decommissioning account must be funded in the amount and according to the payment schedule approved by BOEM; BOEM will estimate decommissioning costs including site clearance. Subject to BOEM approval, a decommissioning account may be funded in whole or in part during the operations period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BOEM control over estimates and approval of funding schedule means lessees must obtain BOEM sign-off for account size and timing; partial/ongoing funding during operations is permitted with BOEM approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminating period of liability for surety — procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.532(a–b): Terminating the period of liability ends the period during which surety liability accrues. The surety must submit its request to terminate to BOEM and notify you at least 90 days before proposed termination; if you intend to continue activities you must provide replacement financial assurance of equivalent or greater value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lessee/operator responsibility to secure replacement assurance if operations continue; surety termination requires notice and BOEM acceptance of replacement prior to operations continuing.

rubrics_metrics.name: How a surety obtains cancellation of financial assurance
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.533: BOEM will relieve a surety from liability for accrued obligations on the earliest to occur of: (a) BOEM determines there are no outstanding obligations covered; (b) BOEM accepts replacement assurance equal or greater than amount to cover period prior to termination or new surety expressly assumes all outstanding liabilities; (c) seven years elapsed since termination if new surety did not assume accrued obligations; or (d) a longer period necessary to complete appeals or litigation related to liabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surety cancellation depends on BOEM's determination about outstanding obligations, replacement assurances, or statutory waiting periods tied to appeals/litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: When BOEM will cancel financial assurance
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.534(a–b): BOEM will not cancel certain financial assurances until seven years after all operations and activities under the lease or grant cease (including decommissioning and site clearance), or longer as necessary for appeals/litigation. BOEM may reduce or cancel if it determines full amount no longer needed. BOEM may reinstate financial assurance if payments are rescinded/repayable or representations of discharged obligations were materially false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cancellation is conservative and protective of future or latent liabilities; BOEM retains post-cancellation reinstatement authority in fraud/insolvency scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOEM may call for forfeiture of financial assurance on default
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.535(a)(2): BOEM may call for forfeiture of all or part of your financial assurance if you default on one of the conditions under which BOEM accepted your financial assurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forfeiture is a remedy linked to breach of conditions that supported acceptance of the security instrument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plans and information required before conducting activities
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.600(a): Before conducting activities on your lease or grant you must submit and receive BOEM approval of the appropriate plan: SAP (site assessment with engineered foundations), COP (construction of facilities for commercial operations), or GAP (activities on limited lease or grant) as set forth in §§585.605–585.613 (SAP), §§585.620–585.629 (COP), and §§585.640–585.648 (GAP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific plan type is triggered by the activity type (site assessment vs construction vs limited lease/grant activities); BOEM approval is required before conducting the associated activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: BOEM waiver of certain information or analyses in proposed plans
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.600(b): BOEM may waive certain types of information or analyses normally required in a plan when you demonstrate that: (1) sufficient applicable information or analysis is readily available to BOEM; (2) the coastal or marine resources subject to the information requirement are not present or affected; (3) other factors affect your ability to obtain or BOEM's need for the information; or (4) information is neither necessary nor required for a State to determine consistency with its coastal management program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants bear burden to demonstrate grounds for waiver; BOEM discretion governs waiver approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan submission timing requirements (SAP, COP, GAP)
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.601: You may submit your SAP anytime but must have BOEM approval before conducting SAP-triggering activities; you must submit your COP within 5 years of your lease effective date and it must contain sufficient data and information for BOEM to complete reviews and NEPA analysis (BOEM may require additional reviews if significant new information arises); you must submit your GAP within 12 months of your lease or grant effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines are strict (COP within 5 years; GAP within 12 months); COP must support NEPA analysis and may be subject to additional review if revised or if new data arises from site assessment activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records retention until financial assurance released
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.602: Until BOEM releases your financial assurance under §585.534 you must maintain and provide to BOEM upon request all data and information related to compliance with required terms and conditions of your lease, grant, and approved plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recordkeeping obligations persist through the post-operations security period until BOEM formally releases financial assurance.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAP definition and approval requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.605: SAP describes the site assessment activities meeting the criteria in §585.600(a)(1) that you plan to perform on your commercial lease. You must receive BOEM approval of your SAP before beginning any proposed site assessment activities requiring such approval. If BOEM determines your proposed facility is complex or significant you must comply with subpart H regarding facility design/construction and submit your SMS as required by §585.810.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SAP approval is gating; complexity/significance triggers more stringent design and safety management system requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAP demonstration criteria (safety, compliance, environmental protections, technology, personnel)
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.606: Your SAP must demonstrate that you have planned and are prepared to conduct the proposed site assessment activities in a manner that: (a) conforms to responsibilities in §585.105(a); (b) conforms to all applicable laws, regulations, and lease provisions; (c) is safe; (d) does not unreasonably interfere with other uses of the OCS (including national security/defense); (e) does not cause undue harm or damage to natural resources, life, property, the marine/coastal/human environment, or historic/archaeological sites/objects; (f) uses best available and safest technology; (g) uses best management practices; and (h) uses properly trained personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SAP must address statutory/regulatory compliance, safety, environmental protection, co-use considerations, technology/management best practices, and personnel qualifications—these are evaluative criteria BOEM will use in approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAP submission procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.607: You must submit your SAP to BOEM pursuant to §585.110.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow BOEM's submission procedures (electronic/docket instructions) in §585.110.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAP content requirements — project information (items 1–17)
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.610(a): Your SAP must include, as applicable, project-specific information including: (1) contact information; (2) site assessment/technology testing concept (objectives, description, technology, schedule); (3) operator designation; (4) lease stipulations and compliance measures; (5) location plat/indicative layout (surface locations, water depths, anchors, moorings, existing structures); (6) general structural and project design/fabrication/installation preliminaries; (7) deployment activities including safety/prevention/environmental protection measures; (8) proposed measures to avoid/minimize/reduce/eliminate and monitor environmental impacts (including mitigation required by subpart I); (9) project verification strategy regarding complexity/significance and strategy for compliance with §§585.705–585.714 if complex/significant; (10) references; (11) decommissioning and site clearance procedures (general concepts); (12) air quality information per §585.659; (13) listing of all Federal, State, and local authorizations/approvals required and whether applied for/obtained; (14) list of agencies/persons communicated with regarding potential impacts; (15) financial assurance information attesting coverage by appropriate bond/instrument as required in §585.516 and §§585.525–585.529; (16) information incorporated by reference and public availability; (17) other information as required by BOEM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SAP is a comprehensive plan document—BOEM reserves rights when a PDE is used to define acceptable parameter ranges and may require additional materials depending on project-specific circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAP required survey and investigation reports (geological, biological, archaeological, metocean)
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.610(b) and following table: SAP must include reports documenting results of surveys/investigations characterizing and modeling the site addressing: (1) Geological and geotechnical reports to define baseline seabed conditions, geologic model, hazards, feasibility, including desktop studies, geophysical surveys, geotechnical investigations, and an integrated site characterization report with recommendations; (2) Biological surveys to determine presence of live bottoms, hard bottoms, topographic features, and marine resources including migratory populations; (3) Archaeological/historic property identification surveys with supporting data for NHPA review; (4) Meteorological and oceanographic (metocean) data: desktop studies using hindcast/re-analysis models and field measurements sufficient for design and analysis of wake effects, sediment mobility/scour, and navigation risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey/report scope and resolution must be sufficient to support engineering design, risk assessments, environmental analyses, and BOEM's compliance reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAP NEPA and other statutory information/certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: §585.611: SAP must contain detailed information and analysis to assist BOEM in complying with NEPA and other applicable laws. In areas where BOEM has no prior experience, the SAP must include information on hazards (meteorology, oceanography, sediment transport, geology, shallow hazards), water quality (turbidity/TSS from construction, vessel discharges), biological resources (benthic communities, marine mammals, sea turtles, birds, fish/shellfish, plankton, sea grasses), threatened/endangered species (for ESA consultation), sensitive habitats (EFH, refuges, preserves, MPAs, rookeries, hard bottom, chemosynthetic communities, calving grounds, barrier islands, beaches, dunes, wetlands), archaeological/historic resources and Indigenous traditional cultural use (including treaty/reserved rights), social and economic conditions (employment, infrastructure, land use, subsistence/recreation/fisheries including seasons and locations, minority and low-income groups, coastal zone management, visual impact assessment), and coastal and marine uses (military activities, vessel traffic, fisheries, other resource exploration/development) including a navigational safety risk assessment and measures to avoid/minimize adverse impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items are explicitly listed to support NEPA, NHPA, ESA, coastal management consistency, and other statutory consultations; SAP must provide sufficient detail for BOEM to conduct required environmental and interagency reviews and to inform mitigation and coordination measures.
